title: Every Even Zeta Value ζ(2n) is Irrational — and the Odd Case ζ(2n+1) is Open
description: For every n ≥ 1 the even-argument zeta value ζ(2n) = ∑' k, 1/k^(2n) is irrational, the sharp arithmetic contrast to the parent Basel open question about ζ(7) / ζ(2n+1). Euler's formula writes ζ(2n) = qₙ·π^(2n) with qₙ ∈ ℚ, so ζ(2n) is irrational iff π^(2n) is; since irrationality does not lift through powers, this genuinely requires the transcendence of π (routed through the repository's hermite_lindemann axiom). Includes the reusable lemma that π^m is irrational for all m ≥ 1, and the concrete corollaries for ζ(2), ζ(4), ζ(6). This entry additionally strengthens the headline to transcendence: zeta_even_transcendental shows every ζ(2n) is transcendental over ℚ (scaling the transcendental π^(2n) by the nonzero rational qₙ preserves transcendence), which refines and implies the irrationality result.

meta.author: Euler / Lindemann (formalized in Lean 4 with Mathlib)

mathlibDependencies.description: HasSum (fun n => 1/n^(2k)) ((-1)^(k+1)·2^(2k-1)·π^(2k)·B_{2k}/(2k)!) — Euler's even-argument zeta formula, exhibiting ζ(2n) as a rational multiple of π^(2n)
If r is transcendental over R and n ≥ 1, then r^n is transcendental — lifts transcendence of π to π^(2n)
A real number transcendental over ℚ is irrational — converts transcendence of π^(2n) into irrationality
Irrational x and q ≠ 0 imply Irrational (q·x) — scaling π^(2n) by the nonzero rational coefficient qₙ
A summable nonnegative series with one positive term has positive sum — gives ζ(2n) > 0, forcing the rational coefficient qₙ ≠ 0 without a Bernoulli-vanishing lemma

originalContributions: pi_pow_irrational: Irrational (π^m) for every m ≥ 1 — Mathlib has irrational_pi but nothing for powers of π (irrationality does not lift through powers); derived from the transcendence of π
zeta_even_irrational: for every n ≥ 1, ζ(2n) = ∑' k, 1/k^(2n) is irrational — the general even-case irrationality result

zeta_even_transcendental: for every n ≥ 1, ζ(2n) = ∑' k, 1/k^(2n) is transcendental over ℚ — strictly stronger than irrationality; scaling the transcendental π^(2n) by the nonzero rational qₙ preserves transcendence
zeta_two_transcendental: the classical Basel value ζ(2)=π²/6 is transcendental over ℚ (hence irrational)
zeta_two_irrational / zeta_four_irrational / zeta_six_irrational: the concrete Basel values ζ(2)=π²/6, ζ(4)=π⁴/90, ζ(6)=π⁶/945 are irrational
The nonzero-ness of the rational coefficient qₙ is obtained for free from positivity of the series (ζ(2n) > 0), avoiding any Bernoulli-number vanishing lemma

zeta_even_ratio_eq_rat_mul_pi_pow (0-axiom): for m<n, ζ(2n)/ζ(2m) = (nonzero-rational)·π^(2(n-m)) — the axiom-free structural skeleton beneath zeta_even_ratio_transcendental, recording unconditionally that even zeta values are multiplicatively π-power-incommensurable over ℚ (their quotient is never rational). Transcendence enters only when π^(2(n-m)) is declared transcendental; mirrors how zeta_even_eq_rat_mul_pi_pow isolates the axiom for single values

zeta_even_finset_prod_eq_rat_mul_pi_pow (0-axiom): for an arbitrary finite family (f i)_{i∈s} of positive indices, ∏_{i∈s} ζ(2 f i) = (nonzero-rational)·π^(2 ∑_{i∈s} f i) — the Finset generalisation of the pairwise product identity, proved by induction on s. Shows the class ℚ∖{0}·π^(even) housing the even zeta values is closed under ALL finite products, not merely two factors; uses only Euler's closed form, no hermite_lindemann

zeta_even_finset_prod_transcendental: any finite product ∏_{i∈s} ζ(2 f i) over a nonempty family of positive indices is transcendental over ℚ (its π-exponent 2∑ f i ≥ 2 is positive) — the Finset companion of zeta_even_product_transcendental, showing no finite product of even zeta values can be algebraic

transcendental_aeval_pi: master engine — every nonconstant ℚ-polynomial of π is transcendental over ℚ (via Transcendental.aeval + pi_transcendental_over_rationals); covers arbitrary rational polynomial combinations of π-powers, not just the monomials q·π^m handled by the multiplicative engines.

zeta_even_add_transcendental: for m<n, the SUM ζ(2n)+ζ(2m)=qₙ·π^(2n)+qₘ·π^(2m) is transcendental over ℚ — the additive frontier, escaping the single-π-power class ℚ∖{0}·π^(even) that houses all the multiplicative results; proved via transcendental_aeval_pi on the two-term polynomial of distinct even degrees.
zeta_two_add_zeta_four_transcendental: concrete instance ζ(2)+ζ(4)=π²/6+π⁴/90 transcendental over ℚ.
transcendental_add_ratCast (0-axiom): additive companion of transcendental_ratCast_mul — adding any rational preserves transcendence (x=(x+q)−q difference of algebraics).
zeta_even_add_ratCast_transcendental: rational shifts ζ(2n)+q are transcendental over ℚ — additive analogue of the ℚ*-scaling closure zeta_even_ratCast_mul_transcendental.

meta.assumptions: Depends on the axiom hermite_lindemann (Lindemann–Weierstrass theorem, giving transcendence of π), imported via Proofs.PiTranscendental. Mathlib does not yet contain a complete Lindemann–Weierstrass development, and irrationality of π^(2n) provably requires transcendence of π (irrational_pi alone is insufficient, as irrationality does not lift through powers). Everything else is machine-checked with 0 sorries.

overview.historicalContext: Euler (1735–1740) evaluated every even zeta value ζ(2n) = (−1)^{n+1} B_{2n}(2π)^{2n}/(2(2n)!), a rational multiple of π^{2n}. Lindemann proved π transcendental in 1882, which immediately makes each ζ(2n) irrational (indeed transcendental). The odd values behave completely differently: ζ(3) was proved irrational by Apéry (1979) — still the only individual odd value known — Ball–Rivoal (2001) showed infinitely many ζ(2n+1) are irrational, and Rivoal–Zudilin showed at least one of ζ(5), ζ(7), ζ(9), ζ(11) is irrational, but the irrationality of any single ζ(2n+1) with n ≥ 2, such as ζ(7), remains open. This entry formalizes the tractable even side and records the open odd side as the sharp contrast.
overview.problemStatement:
**Open Question (basel-problem-oq-01-oq-02)**: Is ζ(7) irrational? Is ζ(2n+1) irrational for every n ≥ 1?

**Status of the question**: genuinely OPEN in mathematics — no individual ζ(2n+1) with n ≥ 2 is known to be irrational.

**What is formalized here**: the sharp even-case counterpoint. `zeta_even_irrational` proves that for every n ≥ 1, ζ(2n) = ∑' k, 1/k^(2n) is irrational, via Euler's formula ζ(2n) = qₙ·π^(2n) (qₙ ∈ ℚ∖{0}) and the transcendence of π. The concrete corollaries `zeta_two/four/six_irrational` and the reusable `pi_pow_irrational` (Irrational π^m for all m ≥ 1) are included.
overview.text: Every even zeta value ζ(2n) is irrational, proved from Euler's closed form ζ(2n) = qₙ·π^(2n) and the transcendence of π; the odd case ζ(2n+1) is left open, as it is in mathematics.
overview.proofStrategy:
**Proof strategy: reduce even-zeta irrationality to transcendence of π.**

1. **π^m is irrational (m ≥ 1).** `pi_transcendental_over_rationals` (over ℚ, from the `hermite_lindemann` axiom) combined with `Transcendental.pow` gives `Transcendental ℚ (π^m)`, and `Transcendental.irrational` converts this to `Irrational (π^m)`. Crucially `irrational_pi` alone does NOT suffice: irrationality is not preserved by powers (√2), so transcendence is genuinely needed.
2. **Euler's closed form.** `hasSum_zeta_nat` at k = n gives ζ(2n) = (−1)^{n+1}·2^{2n−1}·π^{2n}·B_{2n}/(2n)!. Collecting the non-π factors into a single rational qₙ ∈ ℚ, ζ(2n) = ↑qₙ · π^{2n}; the identity is closed by `push_cast; ring`.
3. **qₙ ≠ 0 for free.** Rather than invoking a Bernoulli-number vanishing lemma, positivity `Summable.tsum_pos` gives ζ(2n) > 0 (its k = 1 term is 1), so if qₙ were 0 the product ↑qₙ·π^{2n} = 0 would contradict positivity.
4. **Finish.** `Irrational.ratCast_mul` scales the irrational π^{2n} by the nonzero rational qₙ, yielding `Irrational (ζ(2n))`.
keyInsights: **Even zeta irrationality is exactly transcendence of π.** Since ζ(2n) = qₙ·π^{2n} with qₙ ∈ ℚ∖{0}, ζ(2n) irrational ⟺ π^{2n} irrational, and π^{2n} irrational genuinely needs π transcendental — `irrational_pi` does not lift through powers.
**Positivity replaces the Bernoulli-vanishing lemma.** The rational coefficient qₙ is nonzero simply because the series is positive; no appeal to B_{2n} ≠ 0 is required.

**The even/odd contrast is the whole point.** Every even value is a transparent rational multiple of a power of π and hence irrational; the odd values ζ(2n+1) resist all current techniques past Apéry's ζ(3).

**Honest ceiling.** This result is `axiomatized`, not `verified`: it rests on `hermite_lindemann` because a full Lindemann–Weierstrass theorem is not yet in Mathlib. The dependence is unavoidable given the reduction to transcendence of π.

**A full field-operation closure, not a single theorem.** Past the headline irrationality result the file builds out the entire algebra of the even zeta values under +, −, ×, ÷: products (`zeta_even_product_transcendental`), powers, ℚ*-scaling, finite/weighted Finset products, sums and differences of distinct values, rational shifts, and reciprocals (`zeta_even_inv_transcendental`) are all shown transcendental over ℚ. Two master engines unify the whole family — `transcendental_aeval_pi` (via `Transcendental.aeval`) for polynomials in π, and its single-value analogue `zeta_even_aeval_transcendental` for polynomials in one ζ(2n) — so every rational-polynomial combination of even zeta values, not just the monomials qₙ·π^{2n}, is covered by one proof.
prerequisites: Infinite sums / tsum and HasSum in Mathlib
The Riemann zeta function and its even-argument values (Euler's formula)
Transcendental and algebraic numbers; the transcendence of π
Irrational numbers and their behaviour under rational scaling

sections.title: Module Header and Setup
sections.summary: Module docstring stating the even/odd contrast, why the result is axiomatized (transcendence of π, hermite_lindemann), and the three-step approach; imports of ZetaValues, the Irrational library, and Proofs.PiTranscendental; open Real and the namespace declaration.
sections.mathContext: The even values ζ(2n) are rational multiples of π^{2n}; the odd values ζ(2n+1) are arithmetically intractable past ζ(3).

sections.title: Euler's Structure Theorem (Axiom-Free Skeleton)
sections.summary: zeta_even_eq_rat_mul_pi_pow: for n ≥ 1 there is qₙ ∈ ℚ∖{0} with ∑' k, 1/k^(2n) = qₙ·π^(2n). Uses only Mathlib's Bernoulli closed form (hasSum_zeta_nat) plus strict positivity (Summable.tsum_pos forces qₙ ≠ 0) — NO hermite_lindemann. This is the unconditional backbone under every result below.
sections.mathContext: The 'rational multiple of π^(2n)' structure is unconditional; only the final step 'rational multiple ⟹ irrational/transcendental' needs transcendence of π. This lemma marks that sharp boundary.

sections.title: Powers of π are Irrational
sections.summary: pi_pow_irrational: Irrational (π^m) for every m ≥ 1, from Transcendental ℚ π (via pi_transcendental_over_rationals / hermite_lindemann) through Transcendental.pow and Transcendental.irrational.
sections.mathContext: Irrational(π^m) for all m ≥ 1 — absent from Mathlib, since irrationality is not closed under powers and this genuinely needs transcendence of π.

sections.title: Every Even Zeta Value is Irrational
sections.summary: zeta_even_irrational: for n ≥ 1, ζ(2n) = ∑' k, 1/k^(2n) is irrational. Combines the axiom-free structure zeta_even_eq_rat_mul_pi_pow with pi_pow_irrational and Irrational.ratCast_mul.
sections.mathContext: ζ(2n) = qₙ·π^{2n} with qₙ ∈ ℚ∖{0}; irrational because π^{2n} is.

sections.title: The Concrete Values ζ(2), ζ(4), ζ(6)
sections.summary: zeta_two_irrational, zeta_four_irrational, zeta_six_irrational specialise the main theorem to n = 1, 2, 3, giving irrationality of π²/6, π⁴/90, π⁶/945.
sections.mathContext: The classical Basel value ζ(2) = π²/6 and its successors ζ(4) = π⁴/90, ζ(6) = π⁶/945 are all irrational.

sections.title: Transcendence of Every Even Zeta Value
sections.summary: zeta_even_transcendental strengthens the headline from irrational to transcendental over ℚ: scaling the transcendental π^(2n) by the nonzero rational qₙ preserves transcendence (an algebraic qₙ·π^(2n) would force π^(2n) = qₙ⁻¹·(qₙ·π^(2n)) algebraic). zeta_two_transcendental is the concrete Basel value.
sections.mathContext: Transcendence over ℚ implies irrationality (Transcendental.irrational), so this refines zeta_even_irrational; ζ(2) = π²/6 is transcendental.

sections.title: Scaling Engine and Ratios of Distinct Values
sections.summary: transcendental_ratCast_mul: the reusable engine that q·x stays transcendental for q ∈ ℚ∖{0}. zeta_even_ratio_eq_rat_mul_pi_pow (axiom-free) shows ζ(2n)/ζ(2m) = (qₙ/qₘ)·π^(2(n−m)) for m<n; zeta_even_ratio_transcendental and the concrete ζ(4)/ζ(2)=π²/15 follow.
sections.mathContext: The even zeta values are multiplicatively π-power-incommensurable over ℚ: their quotient always carries a leftover nonzero even power of π, so it is never a mere rational.

sections.title: Products and Cross-Power Dependence
sections.summary: zeta_even_product_eq_rat_mul_pi_pow / zeta_even_product_transcendental: ζ(2n)·ζ(2m) = (qₙqₘ)·π^(2n+2m). zeta_even_cross_pow_ratio_rational and zeta_even_cross_pow_proportional: ζ(2n)^m/ζ(2m)^n ∈ ℚ (crossing exponents cancels π exactly), the concrete witness of algebraic dependence. zeta_even_div_pi_pow_rational: dividing by the matching π^(2n) returns to ℚ.
sections.mathContext: The even zeta values live in the transcendence-degree-1 field ℚ(π): products add π-powers, and crossed exponents make any two rationally proportional — all inside ℚ∖{0}·π^(even).

sections.title: Powers of Even Zeta Values
sections.summary: zeta_even_pow_eq_rat_mul_pi_pow / zeta_even_pow_transcendental: ζ(2n)^j = qₙ^j·π^(2nj), so every positive power is transcendental (ζ(2)² = π⁴/36, ζ(2)³ = π⁶/216). zeta_two_sq_transcendental is the concrete case; transcendental_div_ratCast is the division companion of the scaling engine.
sections.mathContext: The class ℚ∖{0}·π^(even>0) housing the even zeta values is closed under taking positive integer powers, not merely pairwise products.

sections.title: ℚ*-Scaling Closure
sections.summary: zeta_even_ratCast_mul_eq_rat_mul_pi_pow (axiom-free) and zeta_even_ratCast_mul_transcendental: multiplying ζ(2n) by any c ∈ ℚ∖{0} gives (c·qₙ)·π^(2n), again a nonzero-rational multiple of the same π-power, hence transcendental.
sections.mathContext: Together with products and powers this completes the multiplicative picture: the even zeta values sit in a set closed under ℚ*-scaling, products, and powers.

sections.title: Finite and Weighted Products (Finset Generalizations)
sections.summary: zeta_even_finset_prod_eq_rat_mul_pi_pow / _transcendental: ∏_{i∈s} ζ(2 f i) = (∏ q_{f i})·π^(2 ∑ f i), so no finite product of even zeta values is algebraic. zeta_even_weighted_prod_eq_rat_mul_pi_pow / _transcendental generalise further to arbitrary monomials ∏ ζ(2 f i)^(g i). Both proved by Finset.induction_on.
sections.mathContext: The class ℚ∖{0}·π^(even) is closed under every monomial in the even zeta values — arbitrary finite products of arbitrary powers — the Finset closure of the pairwise and power identities.

sections.title: Master Polynomial Engine and Additive Frontier (Sums)
sections.summary: transcendental_aeval_pi: every nonconstant f ∈ ℚ[X] has f(π) transcendental (via Transcendental.aeval). zeta_even_add_transcendental: ζ(2n)+ζ(2m) (m<n) is a two-term polynomial in π of distinct even degrees, hence transcendental — the additive frontier escaping the single-π-power class. zeta_two_add_zeta_four_transcendental is concrete.
sections.mathContext: A sum of two distinct even zeta values is no longer a monomial q·π^m, so it leaves ℚ∖{0}·π^(even) and genuinely needs the full polynomial engine rather than a lone Transcendental.pow.

sections.title: Rational Shifts and Single-Value Polynomials
sections.summary: transcendental_add_ratCast / zeta_even_add_ratCast_transcendental: adding any rational preserves transcendence, so ζ(2n)+q is transcendental. zeta_even_aeval_transcendental: every nonconstant ℚ-polynomial of a single even zeta value is transcendental, unifying the power/scaling/shift closures and reaching mixed polynomials like X²+X (concrete: ζ(2)²+ζ(2)).
sections.mathContext: The single-value analogue of transcendental_aeval_pi: f(ζ(2n)) is transcendental for every nonconstant f ∈ ℚ[X], subsuming the shape-specific closures and covering mixed expressions.

sections.title: Differences of Distinct Values
sections.summary: zeta_even_sub_transcendental: the subtractive companion of the sum result — ζ(2n)−ζ(2m) = qₙ·π^(2n) + (−qₘ)·π^(2m) is a nonconstant two-term polynomial in π, hence transcendental. zeta_four_sub_zeta_two_transcendental is concrete.
sections.mathContext: Both the sum and the difference of two distinct even zeta values escape the single-π-power class and require the polynomial engine, closing the two-value ± frontier.

sections.title: Rational Subtraction Shifts and Reciprocals
sections.summary: transcendental_sub_ratCast / zeta_even_sub_ratCast_transcendental: ζ(2n)−q is transcendental. transcendental_inv / zeta_even_inv_transcendental: 1/ζ(2n) = qₙ⁻¹·π^(−2n) is transcendental (via IsAlgebraic.inv_iff), with concrete 1/ζ(2)=6/π². Together these close the field operations (+, −, ×, ⁻¹) on the even zeta values.
sections.mathContext: Every field operation applied to the even zeta values keeps the result transcendental over ℚ — the full field-operation closure.

sections.title: The Open Odd Case (Documentation Only)
sections.summary: Documentation-only section: no irrationality theorem is stated for ζ(2n+1), because that is the parent open question and is beyond current mathematics for every individual value past ζ(3); closes the namespace.
sections.mathContext: Irrationality of ζ(7) and of every individual ζ(2n+1) with n ≥ 2 is an open problem.

crossReferences.description: The parent entry poses the open question about odd zeta values ζ(2n+1); this entry answers the tractable even-case counterpoint and frames the odd case as open
The Basel problem proves ζ(2) = π²/6; this entry proves that value (and every even ζ(2n)) is irrational, using the transcendence of π
The ζ(6) = π⁶/945 entry computes the even-zeta value; this entry proves it (and all even values) irrational

conclusion.summary: Formalizes that every even zeta value ζ(2n) = ∑' k, 1/k^(2n) (n ≥ 1) is irrational — including ζ(2)=π²/6, ζ(4)=π⁴/90, ζ(6)=π⁶/945 — together with the reusable lemma that π^m is irrational for all m ≥ 1. The result is axiomatized: it rests on the transcendence of π (hermite_lindemann), which is genuinely required because irrationality does not lift through powers. It is the sharp arithmetic contrast to the parent open question on odd values ζ(2n+1), which remains unsolved for every individual value past Apéry's ζ(3).
conclusion.implications: Separates the tractable even side of zeta irrationality (a transparent consequence of π's transcendence) from the open odd side. The reusable pi_pow_irrational lemma fills a small Mathlib gap (Irrational π^m for all m). The positivity trick for nonzero-ness of the rational coefficient is a clean template for any 'rational multiple of an irrational' argument.
openQuestions: Is ζ(7) irrational? More generally, is any single ζ(2n+1) with n ≥ 2 irrational? (Open in mathematics; not attackable in Mathlib — even Apéry's ζ(3) is not formalized.)
Formalize the transcendence of every even zeta value ζ(2n) (strengthening irrationality), a direct consequence of the same transcendence-of-π chain via Transcendental.ratCast_mul-style scaling.
